question: A pile driver accelerates a hammer of mass 125 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 5x between x = 1 and x = 3. The winch must supply the force that gives that hammer that acceleration, and 13 N of cable preload is added to it. The log writes that loaded force in kilonewtons, then subtracts 15 in those same kilonewton units as the leader tare. Two rigs work the site, so the site figure is 2 times the corrected value. The site's fuel bowser holds 450 L, which is not involved. What is the site figure, in kN?

A quarry sheet ends with one number in newtons. A skip of mass 67 kg is accelerated up the incline. The control number is the smaller root of x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0; multiplying that root by 4 and then adding 27 gives the skip's acceleration in metres per second squared. The haul rope must supply the force that gives that skip that acceleration, from which 26 N is subtracted for the guide roller. Nine skips run on the incline, so the incline total is 9 times the corrected single-skip force. A 500 L water tank stands at the head of the incline and is not involved. What number ends the sheet, in N?

A cable-car record ends with one number in kilojoules. A cabin whose mass plate reads 43000 g moves along the line. The exact area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 3x between x = 1 and x = 2 is taken first, and adding 18 to that area gives the cabin's speed in metres per second. The energy the moving cabin carries is the base value, which the record writes in kilojoules. To that record 12 is added, in those same kilojoule units, as the drive-house allowance. What number ends the record, in kJ?

A dock crane accelerates a grab of mass 74 kg at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0. The hoist must supply the force that gives that grab that acceleration. Nine grabs work a berth, so the berth force is 9 times one grab's figure, and the log writes that in kilonewtons. The port has 8 identical berths. A 700 L fuel drum sits on the quay and is not involved. What is the port total, in kN?

A press report ends with one number in kilonewtons. A ram whose mass plate reads 176000 g is driven along its stroke. The control curve is y = 3x^3 - 4x^2, and the acceleration applied to the ram, in metres per second squared, is how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 2. The drive must supply the force that gives the ram that acceleration, and the report writes it in kilonewtons. Five presses run in the shop, so the shop figure is 5 times the record; from it 2 is subtracted for the bolster tare and then 18 for the frame tare, both in those same kilonewton units. A 60 L hydraulic reservoir serves each press and is not involved. What number ends the report, in kN?

A mine winder sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. A cage of mass 179 kg is hauled up the shaft. The exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 1x between x = 1 and x = 4 is taken first; adding 18 to that area and then subtracting 11 gives the cage's acceleration in metres per second squared. The rope must supply the force that gives the cage that acceleration, and 10 N of attachment preload is added to it. The sheet writes that loaded force in kilonewtons. What number ends the sheet, in kN?

A bakery tally ends with one number in kilojoules. Two batches of 294 and 286 identical rolls are packed into equal full trays, using the largest tray size that divides both counts exactly. A basket whose mass plate reads 5000 g is then carried at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that tray size. The energy the moving basket carries is the base value, which the tally writes in kilojoules. Nine baskets are moved per round and 5 rounds are run, so the shift figure is 9 times the record and then 5 times that, after which 4 is subtracted in those same kilojoule units for the door gear. The oven is set to 220 degrees Celsius, which is not involved. What number ends the tally, in kJ?

A canoe club tests a boat of mass 29 kg. Its speed, in metres per second, is 2 multiplied by the sum of 3 and 6. The energy the moving boat carries is the base value. Nine boats race in a heat, so the heat energy is 9 times the base value, and the club writes that total in kilojoules. To the record 15 is added for the starting pontoon and then 9 for the finish gate, both in those same kilojoule units. What number does the club record, in kJ?

A cannery report ends with one number in kilonewtons. A filler carriage of mass 59 kg is accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 12x + 35 = 0. The drive must supply the force that gives that carriage that acceleration, from which 3 N is subtracted for the rail drag. Three carriages run per line, and the plant has 12 lines. The plant total is finally written in kilonewtons. A 260 L brine tank feeds the filler and is not involved. What number ends the report, in kN?

A brick kiln car whose mass plate reads 26000 g is accelerated along the track. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 4x^2 + 6x between x = 0 and x = 2. The drive must supply the force that gives that car that acceleration. Eight cars run per kiln and 8 kilns run in the works, so the works force is 8 times one car's figure and then 8 times that. From the works total 8 N is subtracted for the track tare. What is the final figure, in N?

A packing line has one hopper holding 111 bolts and another holding 211 washers. The supervisor picks the largest crate capacity, in items, that would empty either hopper into completely full crates with nothing left over, and the maintenance team then adds 22 to that number to set the release speed, in metres per second, of a test carriage on the neighbouring rig. The carriage has a mass of 8000 g and runs on a level rail, and the bench it stands on is 1.4 m long. The logger records the energy the moving carriage carries, the run is repeated until 9 identical carriages have been launched, and the combined figure is written down in kilojoules. That kilojoule figure is then multiplied by 5 to give the total charged to the shift. What is the shift total, in kJ?

A calibration curve on a lab bench gives the stored charge as 3 times the cube of the dial reading, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the dial reading. The technician needs to know how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at a dial reading of 1.0, and that number is entered as the launch speed, in metres per second, of a trolley of mass 12000 g on the adjacent rail. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded in joules. A brake pad removes 4 J from that figure and a spring kick then puts 10 J back. The same procedure is carried out with 3 identical trolleys and the three results are added together. The bench coil has a resistance of 47 ohms. What is the combined figure, in kJ?

A goods lift raises a platform whose mass is 180 kg inside a shaft 12 m tall. The control panel takes the two calibration numbers 4 and 5, adds them, and multiplies the sum by 5 to fix the acceleration of the platform in metres per second squared. The engineer works out the force the motor must apply to the platform to produce that acceleration and expresses it in kilonewtons. The building has 7 identical lifts, all accelerated in the same way at the same instant, so the total force on the shared frame is 7 times that value. Two hold-down clamps then add a further 4 kN and 7 kN to the frame load. What is the total load on the frame, in kN?

The figure the test report finally quotes is 4 kJ more than the result of taking 15 kJ away from 6 times the energy described below. Between the 3rd and the 4th second of a run, a shaker table travels at a rate given by 4 times the square of the elapsed time plus 4 times the elapsed time. The total distance the table covers over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is used as the release speed in metres per second of a trolley of mass 18 kg on the rail beside it. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The room is held at 22 degrees Celsius throughout. What figure does the report quote, in kJ?

A conveyor controller chooses its acceleration setting from the values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0, always taking the larger one, and reads it as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A pallet of mass 177000 g sits on the belt and is accelerated at that rate. The force the belt must apply to the pallet is worked out and a constant 14 N of belt friction is subtracted from it. The remainder is expressed in kilonewtons and multiplied by 9 because 9 conveyor lanes run together on one frame. A final allowance of 14 kN is subtracted for the support frame itself. What figure remains, in kN?

On a test bench the charge stored in a coil follows 2 times the cube of the dial setting plus 5 times the square of the dial setting. An engineer measures how fast that stored charge is changing at a dial setting of 2.0, subtracts 9 from the number she gets, and uses the result as the release speed, in metres per second, of a sled of mass 20000 g. The sled is released on a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The bench fires 5 sleds in every cycle and the test consists of 10 identical cycles. The coil itself is rated at 47 ohms. What is the total energy for the whole test, in kJ?

The number at the end of the sheet is 7 times the line above it, and that line is 12 times the kilonewton figure worked out below. A cam profile gives the follower displacement as 2 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 1 times the square of the shaft angle. How fast that displacement is changing at a shaft angle of 3.0 is taken as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a slide whose mass is 139000 g. The force needed to accelerate the slide at that rate is found, 17 N of friction is subtracted from it, and the remainder is expressed in kilonewtons to give that figure. The shaft turns at 250 rpm. What number is at the end of the sheet, in kN?

The figure the rig displays at the end is 14 kN more than a value that is itself 21 kN more than 3 times the kilonewton reading described below. A drive cam gives the follower position as 3 times the cube of the input angle plus 4 times the square of the input angle. The rate at which that position is changing at an input angle of 2.0 is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a carriage whose mass is 100 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage to accelerate it that hard is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons to give that reading. The carriage rides on rails 6 m apart. What figure does the rig display, in kN?

A baggage conveyor takes its acceleration setting, in metres per second squared, as the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. A case of mass 26 kg is accelerated at that rate by the belt. The force the belt must apply to the case is worked out, and since 10 identical cases sit on the belt at once the belt load is 10 times that force. That load is expressed in kilonewtons. A steady 21 kN of tension from the drive drum is then added to it. The terminal handles 900 bags per hour. What is the total tension in the belt, in kN?

The number the control log records is 24 N less than the drive force described below. During a pour, a ladle tips at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total tilt accumulated from the 0th to the 3rd second, taken as a plain number, has 3 subtracted from it, the remainder is multiplied by 3, and 8 is then added, and the result is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a transfer carriage of mass 106 kg. The drive force in question is the force that must be applied to that carriage to accelerate it at that rate. What number does the control log record, in N?

The last number on the commissioning sheet is 19 kN more than the kilonewton figure worked out below. A press controller adds its two calibration constants 7 and 13, multiplies the sum by 2, and then subtracts 4, treating the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A tool head of mass 147 kg is accelerated at that rate, and the force the drive must apply to it is calculated. Because 4 identical tool heads are driven from one frame, the frame carries 4 times that force, and the frame load is then expressed in kilonewtons. The press stands 3.2 m tall. What is the last number on the commissioning sheet, in kN?

A test carriage on a linear rig has a mass of 130000 g. A cam drives a follower whose displacement is 4 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the time, and the rate at which that displacement is changing at 2.0 s is taken as the carriage acceleration in metres per second squared. The control computer works out the force needed to give the carriage that acceleration. Because 10 carriages sit on one beam, and 4 such beams share a base plate, the base-plate force is that value multiplied by 10 and then by 4. A tie-down bolt adds a further 12 N to the base plate. If the whole base-plate assembly is duplicated across 10 bays and the loads add, what is the total force, in N?

The value the crane display shows at the end is 28 kN more than a figure that is itself 27 kN less than the kilonewton reading described below. A hoist controller sets its acceleration, in metres per second squared, to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 14x + 48 = 0. A test weight of mass 59 kg is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must exert on the weight is calculated. That force, expressed in kilonewtons, is the reading the chain above starts from. What does the crane display show, in kN?

The number printed at the bottom of the run sheet is 26 J more than a figure that is itself 25 J more than the energy described below. A test cart of mass 13000 g rolls along a level bench. Its release speed in metres per second is found from a cam whose displacement is 4 times the cube of the elapsed time, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the time: read how fast that displacement is changing at 1.0 s, add 26 to the number obtained, and then subtract 29. The energy the cart carries because of its motion at that speed is the energy the chain above starts from. What number is printed at the bottom of the run sheet, in J?

The figure the rig totals up at the end is 5 times a value that is itself 3 times the energy tally described below. On a machine bench a cam gives the follower position as 3 times the cube of the crank angle plus 2 times the square of the crank angle, and the rate at which that position changes at a crank angle of 1.0 is taken as the release speed, in metres per second, of a slider whose mass is 6 kg. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is recorded. The bench fires 11 identical sliders in a cycle, so the cycle energy is 11 times that value, and a resistive heater then adds a further 23 J to the cycle. That cycle tally is the energy the chain above starts from. What figure does the rig total up, in J?
